answer: Make the epoch proof memory-hard, not time-hard: each identity must fill and randomly walk a large block of RAM to compute its cipher, holding the whole orchard of memory live at once. One honest agent rents a single garden of memory and proves once. A farm cannot time-slice that block across a thousand heads inside one window, because each proof needs its full working set resident simultaneously; it must own a thousand large memories at the same instant. Compute rents cheap in sequence, but N concurrent memories is a hard parallel cost head count cannot fold.
